html:
An earthquake and tsunami on 28 December 1908 that destroyed the cities of Messina in Sicily and Reggio Calabria across the strait on the Italian mainland. It is the deadliest earthquake in recorded European history.

The quake struck before dawn, when most people were asleep, and lasted under a minute. Most buildings in Messina collapsed. Minutes later a tsunami several metres high swept the coasts on both sides of the Strait of Messina. Fires broke out in the ruins.

Estimates of the dead vary widely, from about 75,000 to over 100,000. Most of Messina's people died. Ships of several navies, among them Russian and British, came to help, and money poured in from abroad.

The cities were rebuilt with wide streets and low, stronger buildings, and Italy brought in new building rules for earthquake zones. Many survivors left for northern Italy or the Americas. Like the Lisbon earthquake of 1755, it shook the whole continent.
sum: An earthquake and tsunami on 28 December 1908 that destroyed the cities of Messina in Sicily and Reggio Calabria across the strait on the Italian mainland. It is the deadliest earthquake in recorded European history.
